entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Sextus Carminius Vetus was a Roman senator of the Flavian–Trajanic world whose name appears among the Carminii holding consular and provincial posts as the new imperial aristocracy stabilised after civil war. Families like his staffed the Senate while emperors redefined patronage after 69 CE.

Prosopographical traces link Carminii Veteres to ordinary consulships and administrative careers typical of the high Empire’s service elite. They exemplify how Italian and provincial notables locked into imperial Fasti.

Vetus is a representative of the quieter consular class behind the emperors’ fame.
